patch_description: The previous program failed validation for several fundamental reasons: (1) it returned an empty list `[]` as `column_orderings`, which cannot describe the per-row column permutation it applied; (2) `recursive_reorder` built results with `pd.DataFrame(...values.tolist() + ...)` concatenations and added a fabricated `original_index` column, altering row/column identity and dropping columns during merges; (3) `column_recursion` iterated `as_completed` futures and wrote `result_df.loc[i]` with an enumerate index, scrambling row order and leaving rows unassigned (DataFrame was created empty so `.loc[i]` appends in completion order); (4) after `col_merge` it asserted inconsistent shapes and dropped the merged columns from the output entirely, changing shape relative to input; (5) multiple prints of internal state polluted stdout. The fix replaces the entire editable block with a correct, bounded algorithm: serialize cells once (missing → ""), factorize values to integer codes, build at most three cheap candidate per-row column orderings (a global frequency/length-ranked order, a conditional partition tree using length-weighted pair repetition count*(count-1), and a length-then-frequency variant), score each candidate with the exact serial character-Trie objective (sum of adjacent LCPs over sorted serialized rows, computed via C-speed prefix binary search), and return the best. Data and shape are fully preserved: every cell value is output exactly once per row via the per-row permutation, merged-column groups and one-way dependencies are kept contiguous, and the returned `column_orderings` lists are exactly the permutations used.
